summary.oneLiner: RDB Rasayans Limited is a Kolkata-headquartered, BSE-listed manufacturer and merchant exporter of polymer-based packaging — FIBC jumbo bags and woven sacks — running a single integrated plant at Haldia, West Bengal, with roughly 30% of output shipped to European countries.
summary.business: RDB Rasayans Limited, incorporated in 1995 and part of the diversified RDB Group, is engaged in the manufacture and trading of polymer-based packaging solutions, specifically Flexible Intermediate Bulk Containers (FIBC or jumbo bags) and woven sacks. It runs a fully integrated plant at Haldia, West Bengal, that processes polymer granules through to finished, export-grade packaging under one roof. It supplies the Indian agricultural, chemical, cement and fertilizer industries domestically and is a major merchant exporter, sending approximately 30% of its total output to European countries.

Polymer-based FIBC / woven bags: Customised jumbo bags (FIBC) — baffle, circular and U-panel configurations, 500 kg to 2000 kg carrying limits

currentContext.expansion: The annual report describes no named capex project, no commissioning or ramp-up timeline and no rupee capex quantum. The only expansion language is directional: in the MD&A Outlook the Company states it is "aggressively making effort to expand business activities in West Bengal and also all over India" on the back of FIBC bag demand, that it "will continue to tap new global prospects by leveraging its leadership position in the FIBC segment", and that it is "optimistic of increasing its revenue by focusing on plastic processing solutions". On the asset base, the Corporate Overview describes a single fully integrated manufacturing plant at Haldia, West Bengal, which processes polymer granules through to finished export-grade packaging under one roof, with a monthly capacity of up to 2.5 million woven sack bags and 250,000 jumbo bags and a volumetric capacity footprint that has "over the years" expanded up to 8,600 MTPA - a description of capacity already built, not of an announced addition. Supporting infrastructure named at the same site is an internal quality-control laboratory with peak load testing and weathering machines and an air-conditioned clean room for contamination-free food and pharmaceutical-grade bulk bags.

risks.note: The bags are primarily made from polypropylene, a petrochemical byproduct, so the Company is highly vulnerable to crude oil price fluctuations which the MD&A says directly impact profit margins, profitability and pricing. Flagged twice - under both Weaknesses and Threats and Risks and Concerns - making it the single most emphasised structural exposure.

risks.risk: Intense global competition, particularly from Chinese manufacturers
risks.note: Chinese manufacturers possess massive economies of scale and often undercut Indian exports on price, putting pressure on operating margins. This bears directly on RDB Rasayans given the export orientation of its business.

Stricter global regulations targeting single-use plastics and waste generation are mounting, and the Company must navigate evolving sustainability mandates despite the industry's focus on recyclable and reusable bag designs. A regulatory shift against polymer packaging strikes at the product itself.

risks.risk: Stringent international quality and certification regimes
risks.note: Failure to meet strict international safety factors (5:1 or 6:1) or UN certifications for hazardous goods can result in stiff penalties or rejected consignments in global markets - a direct revenue and liability risk for an exporter.

Stitching and finishing processes for FIBCs remain highly labour-intensive; the MD&A states that scaling often leads to bottlenecks in quality control and line balancing, constraining the ability to grow volume without quality slippage. The Company had a total of 89 employees as on 31st March, 2026.

risks.risk: Product performance risk - moisture sensitivity, UV and weather degradation
risks.note: Woven PP bags can be prone to moisture and vapour permeability unless expensive specialised inner liners are used, and prolonged exposure to sunlight and harsh weather severely degrades woven polypropylene, stripping the bag of its load-bearing strength over time. Both raise cost-to-serve or failure risk in the field.

Bags must be stored in clean, enclosed facilities to prevent mould, dirt and wood splinters compromising sensitive materials such as pharmaceuticals or food; reused FIBCs often fail regulatory standards such as FDA food-grade requirements, and unrecorded chemical residues can cause cross-contamination or dangerous reactions.

The MD&A states that mishandling can lead to severe bag failures, material spillage and significant liability, with wrong equipment - lifting by fewer loops than required or machinery with sharp edges - directly causing premature bag failure and product loss. Workplace safety hazards are named among the industry's critical risks.

Under Segment Wise Performance the Company states it is engaged in the business of manufacture and sale of polymer-based FIBC / woven bags - a single product family with no diversifying segment, so every risk above lands undiluted on the whole business.

strategy.body:
